question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. I can't hardly B. believe that C. he managed to D. finish the marathon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is I can't hardly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Hardly' is itself a negative word (meaning 'scarcely/almost not'), so using it with 'can't' creates a double negative, which is grammatically incorrect.

• The correct form should be 'I can hardly believe that he managed to finish the marathon.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Words like hardly, scarcely, barely, seldom already carry a negative sense and must not be paired with another negative (not, no, never).

• SSC frequently tests double negatives — remember: one negative per clause.

 

NOTE

• Parts B ('believe that'), C ('he managed to') and D ('finish the marathon.') are all grammatically correct; the only error lies in part A.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrase:

Negotiations broke down when both sides refused to meet _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is halfway.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom 'to meet halfway' means to compromise or reach a middle-ground agreement.

• Since the negotiations broke down because neither side was willing to compromise, 'halfway' fits the context perfectly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• 'Meet someone halfway' = make a compromise; agree to something that is between two opposing positions.

• This is a very common SSC idiom — keep it linked with negotiation/compromise contexts.

 

NOTE

• 'With open arms' means to welcome warmly — opposite of the context.

• 'Half the battle' means a good part of the work is done.

• 'In the same breath' means saying two contradictory things almost at once — none suits the blank.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Glib
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articulate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Glib' means fluent and voluble but insincere; speaking smoothly and readily.

• Among the options, 'Articulate' (able to express oneself fluently and clearly) is the closest in meaning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Glib (adj.) – smooth-talking, fluent, plausible.

• Synonyms: articulate, fluent, slick, smooth.

• SSC tip: 'glib' often has a slightly negative shade (superficial fluency), but the nearest given synonym is 'articulate'.

 

NOTE

• 'Sincere' (genuine) and 'Forthright' (frank, direct) actually contrast with the insincere sense of glib.

• 'Dispassionate' means unemotional/impartial — unrelated to fluency of speech.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate idiom:

Despite numerous setbacks, she remained optimistic and continued to _____.
option_2: keep her nose to the grindstone
solution_text:
The correct answer is keep her nose to the grindstone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom 'keep one's nose to the grindstone' means to work hard and continuously without giving up.

• As she stayed optimistic and kept working despite setbacks, this idiom fits the sense of persistent hard work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Keep one's nose to the grindstone = to apply oneself diligently to hard, continuous work.

• SSC often pairs this idiom with perseverance/effort contexts.

 

NOTE

• 'Turn over a new leaf' = start afresh / reform behaviour.

• 'Throw caution to the wind' = act recklessly.

• 'Pull the plug' = put an end to something — none matches continued hard work.

question:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "tire" with the same meaning as in the following sentence?

"I am starting to tire of this long journey"
option_1: My bicycle has a flat tire.
option_2: The mechanic replaced the old tire.
option_3: The baby started to tire of playing with the same toy.
option_4: We needed to put air in the car's tire.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The baby started to tire of playing with the same toy..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence, 'tire' is used as a verb meaning to become weary or bored of something.

• Option 3 uses 'tire' in exactly the same sense — the baby becomes bored/weary of the toy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• 'Tire' as a verb = to grow weary or lose interest (tire of something).

• 'Tire' as a noun = the rubber ring around a wheel.

• SSC homonym questions test the same part of speech and meaning — match the verb sense here.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 2 and 4 all use 'tire' as a noun (the wheel component), which is a different meaning from the verb 'tire' in the given sentence.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

Movies, being a potent medium of storytelling, have a tremendous influence on society, determining cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions. Films are more than a form of entertainment; they represent and caricature social values and are a mirror to the collective consciousness of society. Movies can introduce new ideas, challenge old prejudices, and initiate serious discussions on social issues. Legendary characters and stories can touch the hearts of generations, defining fashion, vocabulary, and even ambition. The pictorial and emotional power of film provides a special kind of empathy, taking viewers into other worlds and experiences, hence understanding and expanding horizons. Still, this power has responsibility; movies can reinforce stereotypes, help spread harmful ideologies, or offer unrealized versions of life, and all the more reason to embrace critical interaction with the narratives we watch.

 

What is one of the major influences of movies on society according to the text?
option_1: They only entertain and do not impact societal values
option_2: They determine cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions
option_3: They are used primarily for advertising products
option_4: They focus solely on fantasy and escapism
solution_text:
The correct answer is They determine cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states that movies 'have a tremendous influence on society, determining cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions.'

• This directly matches option 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In RC 'according to the text' questions, pick the option that restates the exact idea from the passage.

• The key phrase here is 'determining cultural norms, public opinion, and individual opinions'.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 contradicts the passage (movies DO impact values).

• Options 3 and 4 (advertising / only fantasy) are never stated as major influences in the text.

• This is the negative outcome described — option 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Negative-effect questions: look for cautionary language like 'still', 'however', 'reinforce stereotypes', 'harmful'.

• The key words 'reinforce stereotypes' and 'harmful ideologies' point straight to option 2.

question: Choose the correctly spelt word
solution_text:
The correct answer is Evanescence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is 'Evanescence', meaning the state of gradually vanishing or fading from sight/memory.

• It follows the pattern evan-esc-ence (like 'quintessence', 'reminiscence').

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Evanescence (noun) – the quality of disappearing quickly; a fleeting existence.

• Related: evanescent (adj.) = quickly fading, transient.

 

NOTE

• 'Evinescence', 'Evaneccence' and 'Evanescense' are all misspellings (wrong vowel 'i', doubled 'cc', or wrong ending '-sense').

question: Choose the correctly spelt word
solution_text:
The correct answer is Voluptuous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is 'Voluptuous', meaning giving pleasure to the senses; curvaceous and sexually attractive.

• It is spelled vol-up-tu-ous.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Voluptuous (adj.) – relating to or characterised by luxury or sensual pleasure.

• Root: Latin 'voluptas' = pleasure.

 

NOTE

• 'Voluptous' drops the 'u' (should be -tuous).

• 'Voloptuous' and 'Volaptuous' use a wrong second vowel ('o'/'a' instead of 'u').

• This question was marked 'Not Answered'; the yellow-highlighted option gives the official key.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Chalk and cheese
option_1: Things that are opposites or completely different
solution_text:
The correct answer is Things that are opposites or completely different.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom 'chalk and cheese' is used to describe two people or things that are completely different from each other, despite superficial similarity.

• Hence option 1 is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• 'As different as chalk and cheese' = utterly dissimilar.

• SSC tip: though both words start with 'ch', chalk and cheese have nothing in common — that is the point of the idiom.

 

NOTE

• 'Similar' (2) and 'complement each other' (3) are the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• 'Tasteless' (4) is a literal trap based on 'chalk' but is not the idiomatic meaning.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A person who is unable to pay their debts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bankrupt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A 'Bankrupt' is a person (declared by law) unable to pay their debts.

• As per the official key, 'Bankrupt' is treated as the correct one-word substitute here.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Bankrupt (noun/adj.) – a person legally declared unable to repay debts owed to creditors.

• Note: 'insolvent' is a close synonym (unable to pay debts), but the marked key selects 'Bankrupt'.

 

NOTE

• 'Debtor' is simply anyone who owes money, not necessarily unable to pay.

• 'Pauper' means a very poor person.

• 'Insolvent' (the candidate's choice, marked wrong) also means unable to pay debts, but was not the selected key answer.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Ignorance
solution_text:
The correct answer is Knowledge.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Ignorance' means lack of knowledge or information.

• Its most direct antonym is 'Knowledge' — the state of knowing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Ignorance × Knowledge is the standard antonym pair tested by SSC.

• Ignorance (noun) = want of knowledge; Knowledge = facts, information, and skills acquired.

 

NOTE

• 'Wisdom', 'Awareness' and 'Understanding' are related to knowing but are not the exact opposite of 'ignorance'; 'Knowledge' is the most precise antonym. ('Awareness', the candidate's choice, was marked wrong.)

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Iconoclast
solution_text:
The correct answer is Conformist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An 'Iconoclast' is a person who attacks or challenges cherished beliefs and established traditions.

• Its opposite is a 'Conformist' — one who follows accepted conventions and traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Iconoclast (noun) – a breaker of images/traditions; a rebel against convention.

• Antonym: conformist. Synonyms: rebel, dissenter, critic.

 

NOTE

• 'Critic', 'Rebel' and 'Dissenter' are all synonyms (or near-synonyms) of iconoclast, not antonyms — only 'Conformist' is opposite.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A person who believes that everything in life is determined by fate
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fatalist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A 'Fatalist' is a person who believes that all events are predetermined by fate and are therefore inevitable.

• This exactly matches the definition given.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Fatalist – one who submits to fate; believes outcomes are fixed and unavoidable.

• Root link: fate → fatalist.

 

NOTE

• 'Realist' accepts things as they really are.

• 'Idealist' pursues high ideals/perfection.

• 'Pragmatist' deals with matters practically — none relates to belief in fate.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

Why was the window broken by the child?
option_1: Why did the child break the window?
option_2: The child broke the window why?
option_3: Why the child broke the window?
option_4: Why has the child broken the window?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Why did the child break the window?.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passive sentence is in the simple past tense, so the active form must also be simple past.

• The agent 'the child' becomes the subject: 'Why did the child break the window?' — correct interrogative active structure (Why + did + subject + base verb).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Passive to active (interrogative, simple past): Why + was + object + past participle + by + subject → Why + did + subject + V1 + object?

• Keep the tense unchanged when converting voice.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 has wrong word order.

• Option 3 lacks the auxiliary 'did' (ungrammatical).

• Option 4 changes the tense to present perfect, altering the original meaning.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

He said to her, "if you can solve this puzzle, I will give you the prize that I was planning to give away all along."
option_1: He told her that if she could solve that puzzle, he would give her the prize that he had been planning to give away all along.
option_2: He told her that if she can solve this puzzle, he will give her the prize that he was planning to give away all along.
option_3: He told her that if she could solve this puzzle, he would give her the prize that he had been planning to give away all along
option_4: He told her that if she can solve that puzzle, he will give her the prize that he was planning to give away all along
solution_text:
The correct answer is He told her that if she could solve that puzzle, he would give her the prize that he had been planning to give away all along..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In indirect speech, the reporting verb is past, so present tenses shift back: can→could, will→would, was planning→had been planning.

• Pronouns change (I→he, you→she) and the near demonstrative 'this' changes to 'that'.

• Option 1 correctly applies all these changes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rules for reported speech: back-shift tenses, change pronouns per sense, and shift proximals (this→that, here→there, now→then).

• 'said to' + object → 'told'.

 

NOTE

• Options 2 and 4 keep present tense ('can', 'will') — no back-shift.

• Option 3 keeps 'this' instead of 'that' and omits the full stop; option 1 correctly uses 'that'.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The less clothes that I made for the wedding have gone out of style.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The few clothes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Clothes' is a plural countable noun, so it takes 'few/fewer/fewest', not 'less/little' (which are used with uncountable nouns).

• In this context 'The few clothes that I made ... have gone out of style' is the grammatically correct and idiomatic replacement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Countable nouns: few, fewer, fewest. Uncountable nouns: little, less, least.

• 'Clothes' is always plural and countable — hence 'few'.

 

NOTE

• 'The little clothes' (4) wrongly uses an uncountable determiner.

• 'Fewer' (2) and 'fewest' (3) are comparative/superlative forms that do not suit this simple statement about the clothes made for the wedding.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

In an act of brazen defiance and indiscipline, the armed forces publicly challenging a notification issued by the prime minister's office to deal with the leak of information, on a report in the respected Dawn newspaper.
option_1: At armed forces challenging a notification issued by the
option_2: The armed forces challenging a notification issue by the
option_3: The armed forces publicly challenged a notification issued by the
option_4: The armed forces publicly challenged a notification issuing by the
solution_text:
The correct answer is The armed forces publicly challenged a notification issued by the.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The original sentence lacks a finite main verb ('challenging' is a participle, not a verb), making it a fragment.

• Replacing it with 'The armed forces publicly challenged a notification issued by the' supplies the finite past-tense verb 'challenged' and the correct past participle 'issued'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A complete sentence needs a finite verb; '-ing' participles alone cannot serve as the main verb.

• 'A notification issued by...' correctly uses the past participle for the passive modifier.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 wrongly begins with 'At'.

• Option 2 keeps the participle 'challenging' (no finite verb) and uses 'issue' instead of 'issued'.

• Option 4 uses 'issuing', which wrongly implies the notification is doing the issuing.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

She buys a new book every month.
option_1: A new book is bought by her every month.
option_2: A new book was bought by her every month.
option_3: A new book has been bought by her every month.
option_4: A new book is being bought by her every month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A new book is bought by her every month..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active sentence is in the simple present tense ('buys'), so the passive must be 'is/are + past participle'.

• 'A new book is bought by her every month.' correctly keeps the simple present passive form.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Simple present passive: object + is/am/are + V3 + by + subject.

• 'buys' → 'is bought'; 'She' → 'by her'.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 ('was bought') is simple past.

• Option 3 ('has been bought') is present perfect.

• Option 4 ('is being bought') is present continuous — all change the original tense.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

The detective asked the suspect how he could have committed the crime without leaving any evidence when the security cameras had been recording all night.
option_1: The detective asked the suspect, "How can you commit the crime without leaving any evidence when the security cameras have been recording all night?"
option_2: The detective asked the suspect, "How could you have committed the crime without leaving any evidence when the security cameras had been recording all night?"
option_3: The detective asked the suspect, "How could you have committed the crime without leaving any evidence when the security cameras were recording all night?"
option_4: The detective asked the suspect, "How can you have committed the crime without leaving any evidence when the security cameras have been recording all night?"
solution_text:
The correct answer is The detective asked the suspect, "How can you commit the crime without leaving any evidence when the security cameras have been recording all night?".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Converting indirect to direct speech, the back-shifted tenses move forward and pronouns change (he→you).

• As per the official key, option 1 is marked as the correct direct-speech version, opening with a question mark inside quotes and using the reporting verb 'asked'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Indirect → Direct: put the exact words in quotes, use a capital letter after the comma, add a question mark for a question, and shift pronouns/tenses forward.

• 'could'→'can', 'had been recording'→'have been recording'.

 

NOTE

• Options 2 and 3 retain the reported past-shifted forms ('could have committed', 'had been / were recording'), which suit indirect not direct speech.

• Option 4 (the candidate's choice, marked wrong) uses 'can you have committed', an unnatural construction.

question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He took his keys and scrawled a few last things on his shopping list.

Q. He loaded his cart with bread, milk, and some goodies while navigating the crowded aisles.

R. He paid for his meal at the register while the cashier's scanner beeped steadily.

S. At last, he made it home, eager to pack and begin the week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is P, Q, R, S.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The logical sequence of a shopping trip is: prepare the list (P) → load the cart (Q) → pay at the register (R) → finally return home (S).

• This chronological order gives P, Q, R, S.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• For para-jumbles, follow the natural time sequence and look for signal words — here 'At last' in S clearly marks the final action.

 

NOTE

• Any order not beginning with the preparation step (P) breaks the natural chronology; options starting with R or S place later actions first, which is illogical.

question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. They believed that individuals were free to make their own choices, but were also condemned to bear the responsibility for them.

Q. Existentialist philosophers emerged in the 20th century, seeking to understand the human condition in a world without inherent meaning.

R. The movement was a response to the moral vacuum left by the devastation of two world wars.

S. This radical sense of freedom, therefore, came with a profound sense of anxiety and dread.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Q, R, P, S.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Q introduces the topic (existentialist philosophers emerging in the 20th century).

• R explains the cause of this movement (the moral vacuum after the world wars).

• P states their core belief (freedom of choice with responsibility).

• S concludes with the consequence of that freedom (anxiety and dread) using the connector 'therefore'.

• The logical flow is Q, R, P, S.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In para-jumbles, the opening sentence introduces the subject; look for the sentence that can stand alone — here Q.

• Connectors like 'therefore' (S) signal a concluding/effect sentence, so S comes last.

 

NOTE

• Sequences not starting with the introductory sentence Q lack a proper opening, and placing S (a 'therefore' conclusion) anywhere but the end breaks the logic.
